caption:
Before you click, look at where a link really goes. 🔗

💻 On a computer: hover over the link and read the address in the corner
📱 On a phone: press and hold the link to preview it

Read the domain right before the first single slash. Look for swapped letters, like rn instead of m.

📌 Save this.

Follow @techmendly for a new tech tip every day.

#cybersecurity #onlinesafety #phishing #scamalert #internetsafety #staysafeonline #techtips #privacy #securitytips #techmendly

scenes.text: The link text can say anything. The address can't.
scenes.say: The link text can say anything. The address can't. Check it before you click.

scenes.title: See the real address
scenes.say: On a computer, hover over the link. On a phone, press and hold it. Then read the address that shows up.

scenes.title: The name right before the first single slash
scenes.body: In mybank.example.com/login, the real site is example.com.
scenes.say: Read the name right before the first single slash. That is the real website. Everything in front of it is just decoration.
scenes.shown: Read the name right before the first single slash. That is the real website. Everything in front of it is just decoration.

scenes.myth: A padlock means the site is safe.
scenes.fact: It only means the connection is encrypted. Scam sites have it too.
scenes.say: A padlock does not mean a site is safe. It only means the connection is encrypted. Scam sites have it too.

scenes.title: Type the address yourself
scenes.say: When in doubt, type the address yourself, or open the official app.
